subject: MAP: staged capacity schedule, pricing tiers and burst guardrails
messages:
From: Celeste Tan <celeste@nymble.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Nymble Sales <sales@nymble.ai>
Date: 2027-07-18T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff & initial sizing request

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — impressed with the latency profile on short-context workloads. Our leadership wants a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) so we can align evaluation milestones with procurement. Key asks from our side: 

- A 6-week evaluation window with a staged capacity ramp (start small, ramp to peak over 4 weeks)
- A committed baseline for production (monthly reserved GPU pool) with a 12-month term option
- Clear burst behavior and clear pricing for exceeded usage (how many burst hours, per-GPU rate)
- A discount cadence tied to MAP milestones (design review, evaluate success metrics, go-live)

Can you share a simple MAP draft and a preliminary pricing sketch (committed tiers + burst rates)? I attached the internal evaluation plan (Nymble_EvalPlan_v1.pdf) for context.

Goal: sign off on MAP and commercial terms in the next two weeks so procurement can scope the PO.

Best,
Celeste Tan
Head of Platform Partnerships
Nymble AI

Attachments: Nymble_EvalPlan_v1.pdf (application-level test lists, success criteria)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Celeste Tan <celeste@nymble.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-18T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & initial sizing request

Hi Celeste — thanks, and great to meet you today. Appreciate the eval plan.

Attached is a one-page MAP template we typically use; below are the high-level commercial levers we propose so your procurement team can see the tradeoffs quickly:

- Evaluation phase (6 weeks): free trial credits + up to 200 GPU-hours of burst-enabled infra for testing (no charges until we cross the trial threshold)
- Staged commitment (three-month ramp within the 12-month reserved term): Month 1 = 20% of target pool, Month 2 = 50%, Month 3+ = 100%
- Pricing tiers: 
  * 4-GPU pool (T4-equivalent) baseline: $X/hr reserved; burst rate $Y/hr per GPU;
  * 8-GPU pool baseline: committed discount applies at >=6 GPU-months;
- Burst guardrails: automatic throttles beyond configured burst hours; emergency overflow to hosted pool at capped rate; reporting + pre-notification when burst > 60% of monthly allowance

I'll need Marissa to run a sizing + price sketch against your expected QPS and average token lengths. Rishi, can you prepare a 3-tier scenario (4 / 8 / 16 GPU pools) with month-by-month spend and the discount schedule tied to MAP milestones?

Celeste — if acceptable I can put the MAP draft into a shared Drive and we can iterate.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_template_v1.pdf (MAP milestones + acceptance criteria)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & initial sizing request — preliminary economics

Team — I ran three scenarios based on the Nymble eval numbers. Summary attached (capacity_estimate_v2.xlsx). Key points: 

- Scenario A — 4 GPUs reserved (expected for early-stage eval): monthly reserved cost = $12,800; burst pool: capped at 120 GPU-hours/month, burst rate = $6.00/GPU-hour
- Scenario B — 8 GPUs reserved (target production): monthly reserved cost = $24,000; burst cap 300 GPU-hours/month; burst rate = $5.25/GPU-hour
- Scenario C — 16 GPUs reserved (high-throughput): monthly reserved cost = $45,500; burst cap 700 GPU-hours/month; burst rate = $4.50/GPU-hour

Discounting tied to MAP milestones (proposed): 
- MAP sign (start of eval): 5% one-time credit applied to first invoice if evaluation begins within 7 days of signing
- Acceptable eval metrics (week 4 checkpoint): additional 7.5% ongoing discount applied to reserved rates from month 2 onwards if metrics pass
- Production go-live (rollout complete): volume-based rebate applied quarterly (1.5% per quarter up to 6% total)

Burst guardrail mechanics:
- Soft throttle and pre-notify at 80% of burst cap for the month; hard throttle after 120% usage of burst cap unless customer opts into emergency overflow (hosted shared pool)
- Emergency overflow price is the highest burst rate + 20% premium; credits considered if overflow results from platform issues

I attached a month-by-month spend model that includes pro-rated ramping (Month 1 at 25% of reserved pool to minimize upfront commitment). Also added an alternate proposal where the first two months are billed as a pilot at a blended rate (50% reserved rate + 50% burst usage) to smooth procurement concerns.

Attachments: capacity_estimate_v2.xlsx

Marissa
Director, Commercial Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Celeste Tan <celeste@nymble.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Nymble Sales <sales@nymble.ai>
Date: 2027-07-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & initial sizing request — clarifications and asks

Thanks, Marissa — helpful breakdown. A couple of clarifications from procurement/finance: 

1) Can we get the Month 1 pro-rate down to 10% instead of 25%? Their concern is cash flow and committing too early.
2) The emergency overflow premium seems steep; can you provide a cap (e.g., $X,XXX/month) for true platform outages? We can accept emergency overflow pricing otherwise but want a safety cap if Redwood routes requests off our reserved pool due to internal failures.
3) Regarding the milestone discounts: can the week-4 checkpoint be extended to a 30-day rolling window (so we don't miss it due to intermittent test flakiness)?

Also, can we get a short MAP I can take to procurement that lists the exact KPIs (p95 latency <= 220ms, token loss <= 0.1%, availability >= 99.5%) and the payment/discount schedule?

On the attachments — please include the blended-pilot billing table you mentioned.

Best,
Celeste

On Mon, Jul 19, 2027 at 08:30 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — I ran three scenarios based on the Nymble eval numbers. Summary attached (capacity_estimate_v2.xlsx). Key points: ...

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Celeste Tan <celeste@nymble.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-22T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff & initial sizing request — finalized draft for procurement

Celeste — thanks for the thoughtful feedback. We updated the MAP and commercial terms to reflect your asks. Summary of agreed items (draft):

- Evaluation / MAP timeline: 6-week evaluation window starting on MAP sign date. Checkpoint window for milestone acceptance: days 21–40 (30-day rolling window around week 4).
- Staged ramping (revised): Month 1 = 10% of target reserved pool (pro-rated billing), Month 2 = 40%, Month 3+ = 100%.
- Pricing & discounts (final draft):
  * 8-GPU target pool (recommended): reserved rate $24,000/month; pilot blended billing (Month 1 billed at 10% reserved + any measured burst), Month 2 billed at 40% reserved;
  * Milestone discounts: 5% sign-on credit; 7.5% ongoing discount applied from Month 2 if checkpoint passes during the 21–40 day window; quarterly volume rebate as previously scoped
- Burst & overflow protections:
  * Burst caps per tier preserved (see attached capacity_estimate_v2.xlsx)
  * Soft pre-notify at 80% of burst cap; hard throttle after 120% unless emergency overflow triggered
  * Emergency overflow premium preserved but Redwood agrees to an outage cap: if overflow is caused by Redwood platform outage and exceeds 100 GPU-hours in a given month, Redwood will cap customer charges for overflow at $5,000 for that month and credit any amount beyond that back to Nymble on the following invoice.
- Acceptance KPIs (for procurement doc): p95 latency <= 220ms; token-level loss < 0.1%; availability >= 99.5% during evaluation testing windows

Next steps: I'll upload the MAP draft (Nymble_MAP_v1.pdf) and the updated capacity estimate to the Drive and share a DocuSign link for the MAP acknowledgment (not a legally-binding PO, but enough for procurement to start the PO language). Once procurement signs the acknowledgment we will activate the evaluation credits and start the ramp.

Marissa — please confirm the blended pilot table is attached and reflectable in the Drive copy. Rishi — please prepare the final version of the SOW language for the 12-month reservation term and the billing cadence.

If this reads OK to you, Celeste, I'll post the Drive links and the DocuSign preview by tomorrow EOD.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Nymble_MAP_v1.pdf, capacity_estimate_v2.xlsx
